summary: This repo exists, but it is not suitable as the base for a legally clean HD remaster. OpenRA2/RA2Web is a GitHub fork of huangkaoya/ts-redalert2 (977 stars). Its main branch is a stale mirror of upstream as of 2025-08-07: 0 commits ahead and 120 behind. DD-Channel/ra2-web is also a fork of the same upstream (0 ahead, 97 behind), so the two repos are siblings with the same content at different points in time. The README states that the code is an AI decompilation of the proprietary Chrono Divide client (game.chronodivide.com), and the code shows it: raw System.register SystemJS modules from the shipped bundle are committed verbatim, many files are machine-translated minifier output, and config.ini still points to Chrono Divide servers with gameVersion=0.65.1. The fork's GPL-3.0 LICENSE is not a valid grant. Upstream itself replaced it on 2026-09-03 with a notice that Chrono Divide-derived material "is not licensed under GPL-3.0 or any other open-source license." Functionally the snapshot cannot be played: Quick Match, Custom Match, Demo/skirmish, Replays, Mods and Options are all "功能开发中" (feature in development) alert stubs. Only the main menu, credits, a file-system browser and VXL/WAV/lobby/building test harnesses work. `npm run build` fails at tsc. Its only value is as a reference for how a Three.js 2.5D RA2 renderer is put together.
license_evidence:
VERIFIED in the clone and via the GitHub API:
(1) /LICENSE is the full GNU GPL v3 text. It was added in commit ab59fb7 on 2025-05-26 ("chore: 许可证", meaning "license"), and the GitHub API reports spdx_id "GPL-3.0" for this fork.
(2) README.md, in the section "📄 许可证" (license), says the project is open-sourced under GPL-3.0.
(3) The same README opens with a disclaimer added on 2025-08-07 in commit cc0e14c. In translation: "Disclaimer: this is based on an AI decompilation of the Chrono Divide client (game.chronodivide.com) … all rights belong to the owner of Chrono Divide … the owner of Chrono Divide has never open-sourced the game client code in any way."
(4) package.json has no "license" field.
(5) Upstream huangkaoya/ts-redalert2 now reports license NOASSERTION. Its LICENSE was revised on 2026-09-03 in commit 898d891 ("Revise LICENSE to reflect copyright holder's terms") and now says: "This repository contains code reconstructed from the Chrono Divide client. The Chrono Divide copyright holder has not licensed Chrono Divide-derived material … Such material is not licensed under GPL-3.0 or any other open-source license." This fork never picked up that change.
(6) chronodivide.com says only "Chrono Divide is a non-profit fan project" and "Copyright © 2018 Chrono Divide". It publishes no open-source license for the client.
CONCLUSION: The GPL-3.0 file cannot license code the fork's author does not own, so for practical purposes the code is proprietary to the Chrono Divide author. That makes the license unclear at best and effectively none.
provenance: Fork of huangkaoya/ts-redalert2, which is itself an AI-assisted decompilation and TypeScript/React port of the proprietary Chrono Divide client. DD-Channel/ra2-web is a sibling fork of the same upstream. There is no original work in this fork's main branch.
provenance_evidence:
VERIFIED:
(a) GitHub API: fork=true, parent and source are both huangkaoya/ts-redalert2. The compare API shows OpenRA2/RA2Web main is ahead 0 and behind 120 against upstream main. DD-Channel/ra2-web is also a fork of huangkaoya/ts-redalert2, ahead 0 and behind 97.
(b) git log: 87 commits, all by huangkaoya <chdhyc@foxmail.com>, running 2025-05-17 to 2025-08-07. The contributors API lists only huangkaoya. The only other author is Cyhan, with 8 small type-fix commits on branch origin/cyhan/dev (2025-06-24 to 2025-07-02). The history is not one giant initial commit; it is a series of large bulk-migration drops, for example bd49b31 "core game engine" (452 files, +41,019 lines) and 845cd06 "buildtest" (138 files, +19,942 lines).
(c) README disclaimer: "AI 对《时空分裂（chronodivide）》客户端的反编译", i.e. an AI decompilation of the Chrono Divide client. PROJECT_CONTEXT_SUMMARY.md is titled "RA2Web React Decompile". It says the goal is to "reverse-engineer an existing JavaScript project" and that the source modules live in extracted_modules_simple/ with a module-dependencies.json. That folder is not committed. The same file says the original used Three.js r94 and loaded modules via SystemJS.
(d) Verbatim bundle code is committed. src/engine/util/RaycastHelper.js begins `System.register("engine/util/RaycastHelper", [], function (e, t) {`, and the same pattern appears in EntityIntersectHelper.js, MapTileIntersectHelper.js, MapPanningHelper.js and WorldViewportHelper.js. src/engine/renderable/entity/TargetLines.ts has a raw System.register block pasted after the TypeScript class at line 284, and that block is what breaks tsc. src/test/Original*.js are terser-style extracts that use `!0`, comma-expressions and single-letter params.
(e) Minifier residue inside the .ts port. src/engine/renderable/builder/vxlGeometry/VxlGeometryMonotoneBuilder.ts is essentially minified code. ChronoSphereEffect.ts has `constructor(e: any, t: any, i: any, r: any)`. AttackTrait.ts has `canAttackThroughDisguise(e: any, t: any, i: any, r: any, s: boolean, a: boolean, n: boolean)`. Across the code there are 102 `!0`/`!1`/`void 0` idioms, 160 `var` lines and 3,613 `: any` annotations.
(f) public/config.ini points at Chrono Divide infrastructure: mapsBaseUrl=//gameres.chronodivide.com/map/, modSdkUrl=https://github.com/chronodivide/mod-sdk, and a comment "# Chronodivide 中国大区专供" (Chrono Divide, China-region edition). public/servers.ini has wolUrl="wss://wol-eu1.chronodivide.com" and gameVersion=0.65.1. Chrono Divide patch notes list v0.65 on 2024-12-21, which is consistent with a client extracted in early 2025.
(g) The credits fallback in CreditsScreen.ts reads "原项目开发 Chronodivide" ("original project developer: Chronodivide").
(h) The OpenRA2 org also hosts a fork called "webra2" described as "网页红警一键部署包 / chronodivide asssets" (a one-click web RA2 deployment package with Chrono Divide assets).
(i) ra2-games/ra2 and TaiYouWeb/ra2 are unrelated. They are a v86 x86-emulator approach running the original executables, created 2026-09, with no shared code lineage.
tech_stack: TypeScript 5.8.3 (strict: false), React 18.3.1 (app shell only; the in-game UI uses a custom JSX renderer in src/gui/jsx), Vite 5.4.19 and npm with package-lock. Rendering uses Three.js 0.177.0 via WebGLRenderer. Other libraries: @brakebein/threeoctree, three.meshline, shader-particle-engine 1.0.6 (which drags in three@0.84.0 and needs a global THREE shim in src/setupThreeGlobal.ts), stats.js, @ffmpeg/ffmpeg 0.12 (wasm), 7z-wasm, @ra2web/pcxfile, @ra2web/wavefile, mersenne-twister, js-logger and public/libs/fsalib.min.js (a File System Access polyfill backed by IndexedDB). There is no test framework, no ESLint and no Prettier config, despite what the README claims. The repo has 973 .ts/.tsx files, about 97.6k lines.
renderer_architecture:
Everything below was verified in code.
- **Renderer:** src/engine/gfx/Renderer.ts creates a THREE.WebGLRenderer with shadowMap enabled, autoClear off, NoToneMapping and outputColorSpace=LinearSRGB. Color management is deliberately disabled "to match the original project"; the original was Three.js r94 according to PROJECT_CONTEXT_SUMMARY.md. Since Three.js r163 dropped WebGL1, this in practice means WebGL2 only (inference from Three.js release history). There is no WebGPU and no post-processing. render() loops over scenes with clearDepth and one render per viewport.
- **Camera:** WorldScene.createCamera in src/engine/renderable/WorldScene.ts uses a THREE.OrthographicCamera rotated isometrically (rotation.x = -alpha, rotation.y = +beta). CameraPan.ts and CameraZoom.ts handle movement.
- **Lighting:** one THREE.AmbientLight (intensity 0.8) plus one DirectionalLight with a shadow map; ShadowQuality maps High/Med/Low to 8/4/2. Map lighting (MapLighting, Lighting.ts) and LightingDirector.ts handle ambient overrides for nuke and lightning-storm flashes (NukeLightingFx, LightningStormFx).
- **Palette pipeline:**
  - src/engine/gfx/material/paletteShaderLib.ts injects GLSL into PaletteBasicMaterial, PaletteLambertMaterial and PalettePhongMaterial.
  - Sprite and tile textures store the palette index in the texel alpha channel (`paletteColorIndex = texelColor.a`) or in vColor.r for voxels.
  - A palette texture holds one row per palette. The shader looks up `texture2D(palette, vec2(index, (offset+0.5)/count))`, and per-instance palette offset and extraLight come from instanced attributes. Everything uses NearestFilter.
  - House colors come from Palette.remap(baseColor) in src/data/Palette.ts, which recolors indices from REMAP_START_IDX=16 into a new palette row. ObjectArt.remapable gates it.
- **SHP:** src/data/ShpFile.ts and ShpImage.ts decode frames. src/engine/renderable/builder/ShpBuilder.ts, BatchShpBuilder.ts and ShpTextureAtlas.ts pack them into atlases drawn as camera-facing quads, with ShpRenderable, ShadowRenderable and AlphaRenderable on top. CanvasSpriteBuilder handles UI.
- **VXL+HVA:**
  - src/data/VxlFile.ts, vxl/Section.ts, vxl/normals.ts (normal tables) and HvaFile.ts parse the models.
  - Voxels become real 3D BufferGeometry through VxlGeometryMonotoneBuilder (greedy/monotone mesher, still minified), VxlGeometryCulledBuilder and VxlGeometryNaiveBuilder, cached in VxlGeometryPool and gfx/geometry/VxlGeometryCache.
  - VxlBatchedBuilder (instanced) and VxlNonBatchedBuilder attach Lambert/Phong palette materials. VxlBuilder.build scales by cos(camera.rotation.y) * ISO_WORLD_SCALE.
  - So voxels are already lit and rotated in real time, not pre-rendered sprites.
- **TMP/terrain:** TmpFile.ts and TmpImage.ts feed gfx/drawable/TmpDrawable.ts, then MapTileLayer.ts (a tile atlas mesh). MapSurface.ts, MapShroudLayer.ts and MapSpriteBatchLayer.ts (terrain objects, overlay, smudge) are composed in entity/map/MapRenderable.ts.
- **MIX, CSF, INI and maps:** src/data/MixFile.ts supports encrypted RA headers (Blowfish plus BlowfishKey RSA), with mixDatabase.ts providing filename tables and a VFS in src/data/vfs. CsfFile.ts parses strings, and IniParser.ts, IniFile.ts and IniSection.ts parse INI. MapFile.ts decodes map packs using encoding/Format80.ts, Format5.ts and MiniLzo.ts.
- **Audio:** Web Audio API through engine/sound/AudioSystem.ts, Mixer, WorldSound (StereoPannerNode), Eva and Music. At import time, theme.mix WAV files are transcoded to MP3 with ffmpeg.wasm (GameResImporter.ts).
- **Video:** only the menu Bink (ra2ts_l.bik) is transcoded to WebM/VP8 by ffmpeg.wasm (engine/gameRes/VideoConverter.ts).
- **Netcode:** src/game/GameTurnManager.ts is literally `// TODO: Implement game turn management logic`. network/WolConnection.ts is a 9-line stub, and there is no WebRTC anywhere, despite the README claim. There is no lockstep in this snapshot, although the sim uses a deterministic PRNG (mersenne-twister, Prng.ts).
- **Particles:** shader-particle-engine is used only in DamageSmokeFx.ts.
- **Removed Three.js APIs still referenced:** the build reports 17 undefined imports for APIs removed from Three.js, such as THREE.Math, Geometry, VertexColors, PlaneBufferGeometry, CircleBufferGeometry, TrailRenderer and LightningStrike, in Projectile.ts, LineTrailFx.ts, MindControlLinkFx.ts, DetectionLineFx.ts, VxlBatchedBuilder.ts and others. Those code paths would throw at runtime.
activity: From the GitHub API on 2026-09-27: 15 stars, 15 watchers, 1 fork, 0 open issues, no PRs. It is a fork (network_count 252 through upstream). Created 2025-06-23, last pushed 2025-08-29, last commit on main 2025-08-07 (cc0e14c, README disclaimer). It carries the same legal problem.
build_result:
Tested with Node v26.0.0 and npm 11.12.1.
- **Install:** `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` succeeded (94 packages in about 1s).
- **Build:** `npm run build` (tsc && vite build) FAILED in about 2s, exit 2, with:
```
src/engine/renderable/entity/TargetLines.ts(553,5): error TS1109: Expression expected.
src/engine/renderable/entity/TargetLines.ts(554,3): error TS1005: '}' expected.
```
The cause is a raw `System.register(...)` minified module pasted after the class at line 284.
- **Vite only:** `npx vite build` without tsc SUCCEEDED in 2.05s (653 modules, main chunk 1.29 MB, BuildingTester chunk 519 KB, 7zz.wasm 1.59 MB). It printed 17 "X is not exported by three.module.js" warnings for THREE.Math (5), Geometry (3), VertexColors (2), TrailRenderer (2), PlaneBufferGeometry (2), LightningStrike, CircleBufferGeometry and convertShpToCanvas. These are runtime-undefined references.
- **Full typecheck:** with TargetLines.ts excluded, tsc reports 1,864 errors across 354 files even with strict:false: 620 TS2339, 564 TS6133 (unused), 186 TS2345, 129 TS2341 and more.
- **Not run:** no dev server was started, and no game assets are present.
feature_completeness:
Checked against the code of this fork's snapshot.

**Not implemented or stubbed:**
- **Allied campaign / Soviet campaign:** NOT IMPLEMENTED. Zero references to "campaign", and there is no mission or briefing code. Chrono Divide itself has no campaign either.
- **Yuri's Revenge content:** NOT SUPPORTED. The importer requires only ra2.mix, language.mix, multi.mix and theme.mix. VirtualFileSystem.ts has a skeletal branch that would add langmd.mix and ra2md.mix when engineType is YurisRevenge, but there is no YR import path and no rulesmd or artmd handling.
- **Skirmish vs AI:** STUBBED. The HomeScreen "Demo Mode" button only alerts "Demo Mode - 功能开发中 需要遭遇战系统和AI" (feature in development; needs the skirmish system and AI). game/ai/Ai.ts is a 10-line INI holder. bot/Bot.ts and DummyBot are skeletons. Any AI quality would be zero.
- **Online/LAN multiplayer:** STUBBED. "Quick Match" and "Custom Match" show alerts. GameTurnManager and WolConnection are stubs, and there is no WebRTC, contrary to the README.
- **Replays:** STUBBED (alert).
- **Save/load:** NOT IMPLEMENTED.
- **Mods:** STUBBED (alert). mods.ini lists Chinese mods, but nothing loads them.
- **Map editor:** NOT PRESENT, contrary to the README claim.
- **Custom maps (.map/.mpr/.yrm):** MapFile.ts parser exists (IsoMapPack5 and similar via Format80, Format5 and MiniLzo). There is no map selection screen and no .yrm handling.
- **Fog and shroud:** MapShroudLayer.ts exists, but it is not reachable from any game screen.
- **Performance at high resolution:** UNKNOWN, because the app is not playable. The renderer uses batching and instancing (MeshBatchManager, InstancedMesh) and octree culling.

**Present as migrated modules but not wired into any playable screen:**
- **All units, buildings and superweapons:** game logic from Chrono Divide includes Game.ts (1,152 lines), GameObject traits (AttackTrait, MoveTrait and others), and superweapon effects (ChronoSphereEffect, IronCurtainEffect, NukeEffect, LightningStormEffect, ParadropEffect). There are 40+ trigger conditions and executors. WeaponInfo.ts is still a stub. Only the BuildingTester tool (src/tools/BuildingTester.ts) renders buildings on a grid.
- **Naval units and water:** ShipWakeTrailPlugin and locomotors exist. There is no water shader.
- **Bridges:** game/map/Bridges.ts and bridge logic in 112 files.
- **Garrisoning:** 19 files.
- **Veterancy:** 39 files, VeteranLevel.
- **Chronosphere, Iron Curtain and special abilities:** code exists as listed above.

**Actually working:**
- Sound, EVA and music systems (menu music and click sounds).
- Menu Bink video, via WebM transcode.
- INI-driven rules: Rules.ts, Art.ts and IniParser are wired, and public/ini.mix ships Chrono Divide's INI set.

**Overall:** only the main menu, credits, the storage/VFS browser and the VXL/WAV/lobby/building test harnesses work.
asset_requirements:
VERIFIED in src/engine/gameRes/GameResImporter.ts and GameRes.ts. The user must supply the original RA2 (not Yuri's Revenge) files, checked against exact expected sizes:
- ra2.mix: 281,895,456 bytes
- language.mix: 53,116,040 bytes
- multi.mix: 25,856,283 bytes
- theme.mix: 76,862,662 bytes (optional; music)

GameRes.lookForGameFiles requires language.mix, multi.mix and ra2.mix. GameRes.ts also checks CRCs for ra2.mix and multi.mix. The user provides them in one of these ways:
- picking or dragging a game folder (File System Access API, with fsalib.min.js as a polyfill),
- or an archive (.7z, .zip or installer .exe, unpacked by 7z-wasm).

The files are stored in IndexedDB. Music is transcoded to MP3 and the menu BIK to WebM with ffmpeg.wasm at import.

The repo also ships public/ini.mix (1.1 MB), public/res/ra2cd.mix (117 KB) and public/general.csf (283 KB). By inference these are Chrono Divide-authored files, which is an extra redistribution risk.

public/config.ini sets gameResArchiveUrl=https://download.ra2web.com/full-pack.7z and gameresBaseUrl=//wyhjres2.bun.sh.cn/. These are third-party hosts for game resources and must not be used.
hd_extensibility:
These are technically plausible hook points, but they are moot for legal reasons (see risks).

1. **Hi-res SHP replacement (Medium-Hard):**
   - Files: ShpBuilder.ts, BatchShpBuilder.ts, ShpTextureAtlas.ts, TextureUtils.ts, PaletteBasicMaterial.ts and paletteShaderLib.ts.
   - Obstacle: sprites are palette-index textures (the index lives in the alpha channel) with NearestFilter, so AI upscaling cannot be applied directly.
   - Needed:
     - a parallel RGBA path with its own material,
     - a separate house-color mask channel to replace the indices 16-31 remap in Palette.remap,
     - per-frame lookup keyed by the SHP name in ImageFinder.ts,
     - larger atlases.
2. **Voxel upgrade (Medium):**
   - Voxels are already real-time 3D meshes: VxlGeometryMonotoneBuilder, Culled and Naive builders, plus VxlBatchedBuilder and VxlNonBatchedBuilder.
   - Options:
     - swap in a smoother mesher, such as surface nets or marching cubes,
     - use vxl/normals.ts normals for smooth shading,
     - load glTF HD models keyed by art.ini image name inside VxlBuilderFactory.ts.
   - The minified monotone builder would have to be rewritten.
3. **Normal/depth lighting for sprites (Hard):**
   - Only Ambient + Directional light exist (WorldScene.ts).
   - Needed: new normal and depth map textures per SHP frame, plus Lambert/Phong-style injection through paletteShaderLib, or a deferred G-buffer.
4. **Post-processing (Easy-Medium):**
   - Renderer.render() calls renderer.render directly per scene.
   - Wrap it with three/examples/jsm EffectComposer for bloom, SMAA/TAA, color grading and SSAO. The linear-sRGB/NoToneMapping setup would need to be revisited.
5. **Water shader (Medium-Hard):**
   - There is no water system; water is static TMP tiles in MapTileLayer.ts.
   - Needed: a water mask from theater tileset data (Theater.ts, TileSets) and an extra mesh layer in MapRenderable.ts with reflections and foam. ShipWakeTrailPlugin exists as a hook.
6. **Weather (Medium):**
   - Nothing exists except LightningStormFx and NukeLightingFx in gfx/lighting.
   - Needed: a screen-space or world particle layer and fog, driven by LightingDirector.
7. **GPU particles and impacts (Medium):**
   - The current particle lib (shader-particle-engine) is legacy (three@0.84) and used only in DamageSmokeFx.
   - Replace it with a custom instanced or GPGPU system, hooked into fx/handler/WarheadDetonateFxHandler.ts, fx/SparkFx.ts, TrailerSmokeFx.ts and Projectile.ts.

Before any of these can be tried, the build must be fixed: 1,864 tsc errors and 17 removed Three.js APIs.
risks: LEGAL (blocking): the repo itself says it is an AI decompilation of the proprietary, never-open-sourced Chrono Divide client. It contains verbatim System.register bundle modules and minified code, so any derivative infringes the Chrono Divide author's copyright. The fork's GPL-3.0 file is void, and upstream retracted it on 2026-09-03.

LEGAL: the README forbids commercial use and names the Chrono Divide author (Alexandru Ciucă in the upstream README) as rights holder. Publishing an HD remaster built on it invites takedown (DMCA) exposure.

LEGAL: it ships Chrono Divide-authored data files (public/ini.mix, public/res/ra2cd.mix, public/general.csf; inferred to be CD's) and config pointing at CD servers (wol-*.chronodivide.com, gameres.chronodivide.com) and at third-party full-game-pack mirrors (download.ra2web.com/full-pack.7z) hosting EA-copyrighted assets.
FUNCTIONAL: the snapshot is not playable. Every game mode is an alert stub, the netcode and turn manager are stubs, there is no campaign, no YR support, no AI, no replays and no save/load.
STALENESS: the fork is 0 commits ahead and 120 behind upstream, with no independent development. The OpenRA2 org shows no maintenance since 2025-08.

BUILD: `npm run build` fails because of a syntax error from pasted minified code. tsc reports 1,864 type errors. 17 imports of Three.js APIs removed since r94-era code (THREE.Math, Geometry, VertexColors, PlaneBufferGeometry and others) are undefined at runtime.

CODE QUALITY: machine-translated minified code with single-letter params, 3.6k `any` annotations and residual `!0`/`void 0` idioms, plus a legacy particle lib pinned to three@0.84. Modifying it safely would be slow.
README MARKETING: it claims WebRTC P2P multiplayer, a map editor, tests, ESLint and Prettier, none of which exist in the code.
score_rationale:
Legality carries the most weight, and it is disqualifying. The project admits to being a decompilation of proprietary Chrono Divide code, the code proves it, and its upstream has formally withdrawn the GPL claim. So the user could not lawfully build and share an HD remaster on it.

Gameplay completeness is near zero in this snapshot: menus and test harnesses only, with every play mode stubbed. Modifiability is poor: minified translation residue, a failing build and 1.8k type errors. Activity is dormant (a pure mirror of upstream, 15 stars, no own commits).

The one point of credit is architecture: it is a readable illustration of a proven Three.js 2.5D approach. That approach includes palette-index textures with a palette-row lookup shader, real-time meshed VXL with Lambert/Phong lighting, an orthographic isometric camera and a directional shadow map. It is useful to study as a design reference, but not to copy code from.

Recommendation: do not use this repo or its upstream (huangkaoya/ts-redalert2, or the sibling DD-Channel/ra2-web) as the base. Prefer a clean-room or properly licensed engine. Chrono Divide itself could be an option only with the author's explicit permission, which other projects reportedly obtained for non-commercial use.
